title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: A declaration whose body starts on the next line had no removal at all. The extent test now walks down to where the expression really ends.

highlights.title: Bodies that start on the next line
highlights.description: `fun f(): T =` with its body below, a call chain over three lines, `val x = listOf(` over four, `get() = if (a) { } else { }`. The extent test asked one question and gave up on a yes; it walks down to the real end now, counting brackets on sanitized text.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A declaration whose expression body starts on the following line had no removal. The walk stops on the first line that closes every bracket the declaration opened, does not end on an operator, and is not followed by a continuation.
A declaration that never closes still yields no fix, rather than a guess.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: On a real 6329 source project: 418 findings, 418 with a fix. It was 8 without before this release, and 66 before 1.42.233. No existing cut moved, checked one by one across both versions.
